beats.text: Maya went full-time: sixteen thousand dollars more a year. Almost four thousand of it never reaches her. Here's where it goes.
Maya is a single parent with one child. Part-time, she earned twenty-four thousand. Full-time: forty thousand.
Federal tax first: fourteen and a half percent of the extra. Twenty-three hundred and twenty dollars.
Then the Canada Workers Benefit. Above thirty thousand six hundred and thirty-nine, it shrinks fifteen percent. She loses fourteen hundred and four.
And from next July, the Child Benefit drops seven percent above thirty-eight thousand: another hundred and twenty-three.
The twist: on her last dollars, about thirty-six cents of each one is gone. Before provincial tax, CPP and EI.
So before you switch, count the benefits, not just the paycheque.
Next: why January's paycheque shrinks. Follow so you don't miss it.
